## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `CRITERION_HINT` tells users to leave out "shall", but the validator still requires "shall" when `require_shall=True`. This review found that one Important defect and no others.

## Changes
The pull request rewords `CRITERION_HINT` and `BULLET_HINT` in `app/criteria.py`. It also adds a one-line root file, `review.txt`, which the pull-request description does not mention.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — Make the hint match the require_shall option — With `require_shall=True`, a criterion written as the new hint says, such as `"- Save the result"`, is rejected, because `accepts_criterion` returns `" shall " in text` (`app/criteria.py:8`). `tests/test_criteria.py:21` asserts that this exact input is rejected. — When the option is enabled, users who follow the hint get every criterion rejected and the hint does not tell them why. — Fix: Choose the hint wording based on `require_shall`, or remove "without the word shall" so the hint is correct under both validator options.
